column1: # Counts from a search of 118 company texts for the names of Chinese authorities beside a chip word, run on Nov 25, 2026 over the texts as they are cited on that day: counts only, no sentence is copied. The texts, in three groups: A, 39 results-call transcripts of Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu (13 each, Nov 15, 2023 to Nov 19, 2026); B, 37 results-call transcripts of JD.com and Kuaishou (8 each) and Kingsoft Cloud, Meituan and Xiaomi (7 each), Mar 6, 2025 to Nov 19, 2026; C, 42 records of four smaller companies: iFlytek 19 (periodic reports, records of meetings with investors and answers on the exchange's platform), SenseTime 14, Zhipu 7 and MiniMax 2 (results announcements, annual and interim reports and prospectuses). 61 of the 76 transcripts are listed in tables/results_calls_read.tsv; the other 15 are earlier calls of Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu, Nov 15, 2023 to Nov 21, 2024. Three checks, each on the plain text of a saved page, the longest one where a page has more than one; for the 76 transcripts the pages as a visitor sees them give the same counts. (1) "same sentence": for each group and each of 14 words, the number of sentences that hold the word and, of those, the number that also hold a chip word (chip, GPU, semiconductor, compute, computing power, Nvidia, H20, H200, accelerator, 芯片, 算力, 英伟达, 半导体, 加速卡, 显卡, the Chinese words in both scripts). The 14 words, each with its full name and its traditional characters: 网信办 (the cyberspace regulator), 发改委 (the state planner), 工信部 (the industry ministry), 海关 (customs), 窗口指导 (window guidance), 商务部 (the commerce ministry) and 约谈 (a summons to talks); their English names CAC, customs, Ministry of Commerce or MOFCOM, MIIT and NDRC; and two general English words, guidance and regulator. (2) "within 200 characters": every match of an authority word of that list, the general word guidance left out, and of those the number with a chip word within 200 characters on either side (the same chip words without compute, computing power and 算力). (3) "government word": every match of a general word for the government or the authorities (Chinese government, central government, Beijing, the authorities, 中国政府, 当局, 监管部门 and others) and of those the number with both a chip word and a word of restriction within 200 characters. Columns: the check; the group; the word; the hits; the hits beside a chip word; the saved ids of those; what those are. Result: 299 sentences hold one of the 14 words and 3 of them also hold a chip word: the general word guidance twice, each time of a company's own spending, and MIIT once, in the ministry's certificate for SenseTime's cloud platform. The second check finds 3 among 232 matches: that certificate, and the United States Department of Commerce twice in one passage of MiniMax's prospectus. The third finds none among 726. So no named Chinese authority stands beside a chip word in the 118 texts but for an MIIT certificate (SenseTime), and the one other body is the US Commerce Department (MiniMax): the two exceptions of OFFICIAL_RECORD.md, section 8. Controls: the same patterns find 网信办 and 约谈 on a People's Daily commentary [cn-acts-peoplesdaily-bjd-20250801], the Cyberspace Administration in Alibaba's annual report [cn-clips-alibaba-20f] and on a press page [cn-le09-hwbusters-tencent-shrugs], and Beijing with chip and restriction words on a saved press report; the word revenue stands in all 76 transcripts. What the table is not: a count of words, not a reading; many of the transcripts mark passages as not translated (tables/results_calls_read.tsv counts the markers), and what was said only in Chinese there is not searched; a run of the same search on Nov 24, 2026 read 119 texts, two of them copies that are no longer cited (one has been replaced by another copy of the same report), so its counts for group C were different; and a word's absence from a text is not a statement by the company.
